title: Lucy (13 December)
hookLine: a Sicilian martyr whose name sounds like light, honored with candles in dark Scandinavia

cards: It's still pitch dark outside on a December morning in Sweden. A door opens and a girl in a long white dress walks in, slowly, because she's wearing a crown of lit candles on her head.

Behind her comes a line of others in white, each holding one candle, singing. Families, schools and churches in Sweden and its neighbors keep some version of this morning. The girl is dressed as a saint.
Not a Viking, not a winter spirit. A young martyr from Sicily, a long way south. Her name is Lucy.

teach.b: Lucy was a martyr of Syracuse, in Sicily. Like Cecilia last week, she is one of the women martyrs named in the Roman Canon, the first Eucharistic Prayer of the Roman Missal.
Beyond her name, her story comes from her legend.

teach.h: HER DOWRY GIVEN TO THE POOR.
teach.b: She decides to give her life to God, and she gives her dowry away to the poor. The young man she was expected to marry is furious and reports her as a Christian.
The authorities try to drag her off to shame her, and in the legend they cannot move her at all. Not with ropes, not with a team of oxen. She stands there like a pillar.
She dies by the sword. Now, the light.

teach.h: A NAME THAT SOUNDS LIKE LIGHT.
teach.b: Lucy's name sounds like lux, the Latin for light, and the people who told her story leaned into it.
Paintings show her holding a lamp, or carrying her eyes on a dish, and she became the patron of people with trouble seeing.
Her feast falls in the dark weeks of the northern winter, and some say that is part of why the north took her to heart. John's gospel puts it in one line.

teach.h: AND THE LIGHT SHINETH IN DARKNESS.
teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "And the light shineth in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it." The Lucy morning acts that verse out.
Somebody walks into the dark room carrying light, and the room doesn't get to stay dark. A martyr who gave her dowry away became, far from home, the girl who brings the morning in.

how: Saint Lucy is remembered on 13 December; in Sweden and other Nordic countries the day is kept with processions of singers in white led by a girl wearing a crown of candles, and in Sicily with special foods and Masses.

games.q: you're Lucy. a dowry has been set aside for your marriage, but you've decided to give your life to God. what do you do with the money?
o: hand it to the young man as a settlement
games.why: in the legend she gives it away to the poor, and the young man, furious, reports her as a Christian.

practice: If you have a candle and it's safe, light it now; if not, sit in a dim spot and switch on one small lamp, and notice how far one small light reaches, and where it stops.
If you pray, hold the people in your life who are in a dark stretch right now, one at a time, in that light; if you don't, simply stay with the glow.
